question: Shan has ₹1612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Piyush and Manoj and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Piyush and Manoj got same amount after 12 and 13 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Shan give to Piyush?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal in CI, the ratio of shares is directly based on the accumulating factor raised to the difference in time.

Time difference = 13 − 12 = 1 year.

Ratio of Piyush's share to Manoj's share = (100 + 8)/100 = 108/100 = 27/25.

Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts ⇒ 52 parts = ₹1612 ⇒ 1 part = ₹31.

Piyush's share = 27 parts × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**
